exports: pub fn validate_nanoid(input: &[u8], len: u8) -> FormatResult<()>

test_vectors.execution: Not run. The task prohibits cargo, rustc, rustfmt, and all build/check commands. Source and deterministic test vectors were reviewed by reading only.
implementation_properties: Only the assigned module and this handoff report were written; frozen root definitions, contracts, dependencies, and ABI files were preserved.
Validators use the frozen FormatResult, FormatFailure, FormatFailureKind, HexPolicy, and HexCase types.
NanoId requires a nonzero configured byte length and accepts exactly ASCII letters, decimal digits, underscore, and hyphen.
Address and transaction hash delegate to binary::validate_hex with prefix=true, case=Any, and exact_bytes=20 or 32 respectively, mapping the successful count to unit and preserving failures.

Length failures precede content failures and use the input-end index; content failures name the first invalid byte relative to the supplied slice. FormatFailure::new supplies saturating index conversion.
Validation uses no allocations, unsafe code, external dependencies, decoding, platform services, or mutable global state, and runs in linear time with constant auxiliary memory.
Public documentation limits acceptance to lexical validity and makes no entropy, uniqueness, chain, checksum, signature, existence, or authorization claim.

cases.coverage: Single-character category boundaries, _-0123456789aAzZ, V1StGXR8_Z5jdHi6B-myT, repeated underscores, all 64 alphabet bytes, and 255 repeated hyphens.
Every configured length 1 through 255 against every input length 0 through 256, using both valid and invalid contents; verifies exact-length acceptance and length-before-content error precedence.
Zero configured length against input lengths 0 through 256, including empty and invalid-byte inputs; all fail with InvalidLength at the slice end.
All 256 byte values at every position of lengths 1, 21, and 255, with membership determined independently from the complete alphabet and exact error indices.

Leading, trailing, and embedded whitespace, CRLF, NUL, invalid UTF-8, accented and fullwidth letters, emoji, nonbreaking space, raw JSON escape spelling, JSON quotes, and base64-only punctuation; confirms lengths count bytes.
Competing invalid bytes, failures at the first and last byte, and a wrong-length input containing multiple invalid bytes.
Concrete 40-digit address and 64-digit hash vectors, zero values, all lowercase and uppercase maximum values, and arbitrary mixed-case hex without checksum enforcement.
Every length 0 through 132 for each fixed format, with both a correct and incorrect first prefix byte; verifies exact 42-byte and 66-byte totals and length failure indices.
All 256 byte values at each of all 42 address and 66 hash positions, including exact lowercase prefix enforcement, all hex cases, non-ASCII bytes, controls, separators, and punctuation.
Missing prefix, prefix-only and empty inputs, appended space, newline and NUL, quoted values, prepended whitespace, and rejection when an address is supplied as a hash or a hash as an address.
Multiple simultaneous errors at both prefix bytes, the first digit, and the last digit, corrected in sequence to verify deterministic first-error indices.

NanoId, address, and hash slices surrounded by invalid sentinels; truncated and empty slices; relative prefix and digit error indices; fixed-format inputs ending exactly at the backing-array boundary.
